title: LazyBarrier: Reconstructing Android IO Stack for Barrier-Enabled Flash Storage
problem: Barrier-Enabled IO Stack (BEIOS) exhibits performance degradation in multi-threaded scenarios because barrier write commands scale linearly with thread count, making it inefficient for concurrent IO operations in Android systems.
motivation: Efficient order-preserving IO operations are critical for data consistency in storage systems, and reducing barrier command overhead improves both mobile and server application performance.
method: LazyBarrier introduces an Order-Preserving Write (OPW) Model based on Finite Automata that defines state transitions for ordering semantics. The Lazy Issue algorithm minimizes barrier write commands through deferred issuance. F2FS is modified to support OPW natively. Barrier Scheduling coordinates ordering in multi-queue block layers.
key_novelty: The Lazy Issue algorithm minimizes barrier write commands through lazy issuance, eliminating the linear scaling of BWCs with thread count.
contributions: OPW Model based on Finite Automata defining order-preserving write semantics
Lazy Issue algorithm minimizing barrier write command overhead
Modified F2FS filesystem supporting OPW operations
Barrier Scheduling for multi-queue block layer coordination

metrics.speedup: 73% over BEIOS (FIO benchmark), 29% in real applications, 19% in dbench

primary_theme: optimizing order-preserving writes in android flash storage
